title: Access logs and monitoring
goal_html: Students practice reading physical access log data to identify anomalous patterns (after-hours access, repeated denial bursts, location inconsistencies) and articulate what each pattern indicates to a security analyst. Ties to LO 2.4.A (analyze access logs to detect physical attack indicators).

steps_html:
1. Each pair reads through the log. For every row, decide: normal or anomalous? Write a one-word verdict in the margin.
  2. For each anomalous row, write which rule it triggers: AFTER-HOURS, BURST, or LOCATION-INCONSISTENCY.
  3. Discuss: which anomaly is the most serious, and what would you recommend the analyst do next?
collaborate_html: Assign roles: one partner is the "analyst" (flags entries and names the rule), the other is the "attacker's lawyer" (argues why the entry might be innocent). After classifying all entries, swap roles and revisit the two most disputed entries.
exit_html: Each student submits: (1) which badge IDs you would report to security, (2) the rule that triggered each flag, and (3) one defensive countermeasure that would reduce the risk each flagged pattern represents.
